title: Adaptive audit shard sparsity & RBAC-aligned partitioning for cost-controlled retention
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Audit event volume has grown 4x in Q4 across multi-tenant workloads. Current ingestion shards and fixed retention windows cause hotspots and unpredictable storage spend for tenants with bursty SSO/saml traffic.

Goal: Implement an adaptive shard sparsity and RBAC-mapped partitioning scheme that reduces cold storage costs and query tail latency while preserving audit fidelity for admins and compliance. This is a horizontal change across ingest, indexer and retention controller and must account for SSO/SAML-derived tenant linking and RBAC v2 identity bindings.

Scope:
- Adaptive shard creation policy driven by tenant throughput, event cardinality and RBAC sensitivity labels.
- Map RBAC v2 role bindings to partition tiers (privileged events pinned to hot shards, low-sensitivity to compacted cold tiers).
- Retention controller changes to support cost-aware tier migration and TTL that can be overridden for compliance cases.
- Instrumentation and billing attribution per shard for cost reports.

Non-goals:
- Not changing audit schema.
- Not tackling full cross-region replication (follow-up project).
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive shard allocator creates or retires shards automatically when tenant 1h moving average exceeds thresholds without impacting ingest availability
RBAC role label appears on audit event metadata and is used by partitioner to route events to correct shard tier
Retention controller enforces tiered TTLs and emits per-tenant cost signals to Console; guarantees for pinned compliance data are honored
End-to-end tests that simulate SSO burst with 100k events/min show <5% increase in 95th percentile ingest latency and 25% reduction in cold storage growth over baseline
Schema remains backward compatible; no change required to downstream compliance queries
Full rollout playbook exists with rollback steps and monitoring runbook entries
tasks: Design: finalize shard density model and RBAC label set (Confluence link in design_links)
Implement: shard allocator service changes and heuristics
Implement: partitioner enhancement to attach RBAC-derived tier metadata at ingest
Implement: retention controller hooks to migrate shard segments between hot/cold tiers based on cost signals
Observability: add shard-level cost/ingest/latency metrics and Console visualization
Testing: unit + integration + chaos tests for shard churn and RBAC mismapping
Rollout: staged canary across 3 regions then global with abort on error budget burn
infra_changes: Add per-shard billing counters to ingestion pipeline (Prometheus + statsd exporters)
S3 lifecycle rules templated per shard tier; cold tier storage class migration
New autoscaler policy for shard coordinator microservice
rollout: Phase 1: enable on internal staging with synthetic tenants (2025-03-10)
Phase 2: canary on 5 external tenants with CSP customers (2025-03-17)
Phase 3: 50% traffic rollout and observe cost signals (2025-03-24)
comments: 2025-02-14 - Priya Nair: Kickoff meeting notes: strong preference from compliance for pinned retention for privileged roles; need policy to override automated compaction
2025-02-20 - Samuel Ortiz: Prototype shard allocator shows 18% reduction in shard count for steady tenants; added RBAC label propagation spike to next sprint
2025-02-27 - Design review: PM Eva Martinez - approve model but request explicit admin toggle in Console for tenant-level exceptions
2025-03-02 - Security review (initial): flagged that SSO/SAML attribute mapping must be canonicalized to avoid role spoofing; added requirement to validate signed assertions
2025-03-03 - Samuel Ortiz: Implemented initial retention-hooks PR; integration tests failing intermittently under high-churn; triaging with storage team
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive compaction reduces cost but increases query latency for ad-hoc audit queries; chosen hybrid approach pins high-sensitivity events and uses probabilistic compaction for low-sensitivity streams
Open questions: how to represent RBAC-derived sensitivity numerically for allocator heuristics; decided to start with 3-tier model (privileged, normal, bulk)
Follow-ups: cross-region replication of pinned shards (separate RFC), expose per-tenant cost alerting in Console (ENG-210400)
